faq.q: Are Princeton homes on town water?
faq.a: Homes inside the Town of Princeton are on the Town’s water and sewer. Rural homes in Area H are usually on a private well and septic system, which you should test and inspect before removing conditions.

faq.q: Did the 2021 flood affect Princeton homes?
faq.a: Yes. In November 2021 the Tulameen and Similkameen overflowed their banks and dikes, and 290 households were displaced at first. Ask about flood history and floodplain status for any home near the rivers.

faq.q: Has Jared sold homes in Princeton?
faq.a: Yes, including a three-bedroom house on Similkameen Avenue and a house and shop on two RM3-zoned lots on Angela Avenue.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

parts.t: Houses in Princeton range from 1910s and 1920s homes on town lots near the rivers to newer houses, mobile homes and cabins on rural land in the Similkameen Valley. This search covers the Town of Princeton and the rural area around it. Jared has sold in Princeton:
a three-bedroom house on Similkameen Avenue
a house and shop on two RM3-zoned lots on Angela Avenue

blocks.text: What to check on a Princeton house

items.t: Floodplain and flood history:
the 2021 flood reached homes along the Tulameen and Similkameen. Ask the Town whether the lot is in a floodplain and check the disclosure.
Age of the house:
many town houses are a century old. Budget for the wiring, plumbing, foundation and roof, and get an inspection.
Water and septic:
town lots are on Town water and sewer; rural houses are usually on a well and septic. Test the well for flow and quality and have the septic inspected.
Zoning:
the Town of Princeton zones town lots; rural Area H is zoned by the Regional District under Bylaw No. 3065, 2024.
Suites:

under the Province’s 2023 small-scale multi-unit housing law, every BC municipality must allow a secondary suite or a detached accessory dwelling on most single-family lots. The three-to-four-unit rule applies only in municipalities of more than 5,000 people, and Princeton has under 3,000.
The 2021 flood:

in November 2021 the Tulameen and Similkameen rivers overflowed their banks and dikes. The Town declared a state of emergency and 290 households (571 residents) were displaced at first. The Province’s summary lists $11.9 million in interim flood support, more than $4 million of it for drinking water repairs, and funding for a flood hazard assessment of both rivers. The Town’s 2024 request for federal flood-mitigation funding was turned down.
